title: Back to New York on the Pantages circuit; one black act per bill
summary: He mentions playing the Paramount with Crosby and Sinatra and says there were never two black acts on one bill.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: didn't pay nothing. What I said -- here's a sad story like every time I think of it I'd almost cry, to think I was robbed of my goodness, same as Buck would have been robbed of his talent. If he had stayed in school with book learning to do what with, get what? Sad. However, from the Pathe' studio we come back to New York. We came back to New York and come back on the Pantages circuit, from New York to California on the Pantages circuit. Now we have already now played the Paramount Theater with Bing Crosby when he first got there, with Frank Sinatra when he first got there, were on the bill with these guys at the Paramount. I was in high society, wasn't I?
Were you the only black act?
Yeah, there ain't no two black acts on no bill. One time in California there was two colored acts on the same bill.
